title: Product configuration
description: Build-time product identity for a platform built on base-services. The ONE place the product name, brand, and legal entity live, so a rename is an edit to one file rather than a search-and-replace across every service. Runtime wiring belongs in env vars; per-customer white-label belongs in tenant-service branding. Copy product.example.json to product.json, fill it, and never commit the filled copy. Validated by scripts/check_product_config.py so a bad edit fails at lint, not in production.

slug.description: Lowercase machine name. Appears in file names and CLI output only — never in a service name, a database, a table, or a token. Empty is allowed in product.example.json; the CI check rejects it in a real product.json.

name.description: The product name as a human reads it. Empty renders as a visible placeholder rather than silently shipping the wrong name; the CI check rejects it in a real product.json.

legalName.description: Registered legal entity, exactly as on the commercial registration, including the legal suffix. May be empty until incorporation.

urls.description: https only. A read-only or externally-shared portal must be its own origin, never a path on the main app — a separate origin cannot be reached by a flag flip or a routing bug.

securityEmail.description: Published for vulnerability disclosure. A researcher, an auditor, and a customer's procurement team will all look for it. The CI check rejects an empty value in a real product.json.

tokensRef.description: Path to the color token file. Colors live there, never here, and never in code.

rtl.description: Right-to-left locales. Must be a subset of `supported` — enforced by the CI check, which a schema cannot express.

timezone.description: IANA name, e.g. UTC or Asia/Riyadh.

currencyMinorUnits.description: SAR/USD = 2. KWD/BHD/OMR = 3. Money is stored as an integer in these units; a float loses a minor unit per operation and breaks reconciliation.

vatNumber.description: Saudi VAT number: 15 digits beginning with 3. Empty until registered. Wrong here means wrong on every e-invoice zatca-service issues.

identifiers.description: FROZEN. These values are written into data a customer already holds and artifacts already signed. A rebrand edits `identity` and `brand` and leaves this block untouched. Changing a value here is a data migration with a compatibility window, never a config edit. scripts/check_product_config.py pins these against the previous commit and fails the build unless the commit body carries a `MIGRATION:` line.

jwtIssuer.description: Change it and every live session and refresh token is rejected.

linkNs.description: Namespace for externally shared links. Change it and every link ever sent stops resolving. Versioned: move forward by bumping the suffix.

signatureDomain.description: Domain-separation string for signed artifacts. Change it and every signed artifact fails verification, forever. A signed artifact is immutable; so is its signature domain. Versioned: a new value means a new suffix, and old artifacts keep verifying against the old one.

rolloutSalt.description: Salts the feature-flag rollout hash. Change it and EVERY user re-buckets: a customer inside a 10% rollout is silently moved out, and one who never saw the feature is moved in. No error is raised. Frozen for the same reason a signature domain is.

items.description: Service names carry no product name. `billing`, never `acme-billing`. The CI check rejects any name containing the product slug — a schema cannot see that, because it does not know the slug.

prose.description: Human notes. Stripped before the object is compared or consumed.

i18nText.description: One entry per supported locale. Every customer-visible string ships in every language from day one; bilingual is never bolted on later. The CI check verifies the keys match locale.supported.

httpsUrl.description: https only. A shared link over http is not evidence of anything.
